title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults, quant-profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Nambiar
ci_status: pass (2 reruns due to flaky scheduling test)
description: Context: we have several manual knobs for batching/caching defaults and quantization profiles that customers and Dedicated deployments repeatedly tune per workload. This PR implements an autotune-first + safe-defaults approach to reduce per-token unit economics by default while preserving latency SLOs. It touches three areas: 1) server/runtime defaults and heuristics for batching and prefix/KV caching, 2) a set of vetted quantization profiles for common model families (Llama2, Mistral, LLaMA-compat variants) with automatic fallback, and 3) a small unit-economics (uecon) toolkit that surfaces expected token-cost changes and provides a CLI to simulate cost impact and suggest profile choices. This change is behind a reversible feature flag (cost_autotune_v1) and includes a clear migration path for existing Dedicated customers. Changes: - Autotuner: new autotune service that observes short-window latency and throughput and recommends per-deployment batching.window_ms and batching.max_batch_size changes; defaults now bias towards slightly higher batching for steady traffic while keeping tail latency budgets. - KV/prefix caching defaults: increased prefix cache TTL for short-lived conversational workloads and improved eviction scoring to favor hot prefixes. - Quant profiles: added quantization profiles q4_0_opt, q5_1_fast, q8_0_prod for tested model families; profiles include memory/latency tradeoffs and compatible kernel overrides. - Unit econ tool: new CLI redwood uecon simulate --profile <profile> --workload <trace> and backend telemetry to compute expected cost delta; dashboard panels for per-model unit cost. - Observability: new metrics redwood.autotune.recommendations, redwood.uecon.estimated_cost_delta, and linked debug logs. - Safety: feature flag, gradual rollout default (10% of traffic), and automated rollback if tail_lat_p95 increases by >15% relative to baseline. Testing: unit tests for autotuner heuristics, integration tests in perf-canary infra using synthetic traces, manual canary on staging with Llama2-13B and Mistral-7B workloads. Migration notes: Dedicated deployments will get opt-in configuration during upgrade; hosted customers see gradual rollout controlled by flag. Related: ENG-1723, PM-214, SUP-439. Checklist: [x] tests added/updated [x] feature-flagged [x] docs updated (docs/costs/uecon.md) [x] telemetry added [x] rollout plan included
